stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude agents found a new enzyme system in DNA data
stories.standfirst: The company says about 950 agents searched sequence databases for 21 hours and turned up a reverse transcriptase next to a repeat array.
body: Anthropic said on Tuesday that agents running on its Claude models had found a new enzyme system in bacteriophages, which it calls array-associated reverse transcriptases, or ART. The company said the system pairs a reverse transcriptase with an accessory protein of unknown function and a long array of evenly spaced DNA repeats.

The search is the company's own account, and no outside group has yet reproduced it. Anthropic said about 950 agents spent 21 hours and 210 million tokens reading a database of DNA sequences, gathering more than 200,000 reverse transcriptases, narrowing those to about 3,500 candidate systems, and writing up the 20 it found most compelling.

The comparison to CRISPR is Anthropic's. The company described the repeat array as "a pattern reminiscent of CRISPR", and The Verge reported the company is comparing the find to the gene-editing tool. What ART does is not established. "Although we don't yet know its function, the system that Claude discovered has a set of characteristics" worth following, Anthropic wrote, adding that its work on the primary function is ongoing.

Human scientists did the bench work, at Anthropic's Bay Area laboratory at biosafety levels 1 and 2. The company said its first experiments show the ART array is also expressed as a set of distinct short RNAs, and said that suggests something analogous to CRISPR may be at play. Anthropic has posted a preprint with the detail.

One outside researcher has commented. Feng Zhang of MIT and the Broad Institute, who worked on CRISPR gene editing, said the identification of RNA-repeat arrays sitting next to reverse transcriptases "is genuinely intriguing and merits further investigation". He did not say the finding was confirmed.

stories.headline: Anthropic opens Claude Marketplace, lets buyers pay with existing commitments
stories.standfirst: The directory lists connectors, agents and consultancies from Cursor, CrowdStrike, Harvey and Snowflake, and Anthropic says an existing contract can pay for them.
body: Anthropic opened Claude Marketplace on Wednesday, a directory of connectors, plugins, agents and service partners that its customers can buy against money they have already committed to the company. The announcement named plugins such as Slack and Notion, products from Cursor and CrowdStrike, and service partners including Accenture and Deloitte.

The marketplace page carries 15 products, grouped by use case. Augment, Base44, CodeRabbit, Factory, GitLab, Lovable and Vercel sit under code, Gamma and Snowflake under data, Harvey and Legora under legal, and Hebbia and Rogo under financial services. Anthropic said sellers can also list their own tools, agents or services.

The pitch is financial rather than technical. "Put your Anthropic commitment toward software that already does the job," the page says, offering to let a buyer draw on one contracted budget across several Claude-powered tools instead of negotiating with each seller. Anthropic listed the benefit as "consolidated AI spend".

How much of that spend transfers, and on what terms, the page does not say. It publishes no prices, does not state which Claude plans reach the marketplace, and points enterprise buyers at a "Request to buy" form. Anthropic did not say how a listing is reviewed before it appears.

stories.headline: vLLM says open-source TPU kernel runs Kimi K3 at 709 tokens a second
stories.standfirst: The project put that against 450 tokens a second on Nvidia's GB200, and said all 92 of the model's expert layers run in one kernel.
body: The vLLM project said on Wednesday that a TPU megakernel open-sourced by the inferact team runs Moonshot's Kimi K3 at 709 tokens a second, against 450 on Nvidia's GB200. It credited the inferact team with the work and said a writeup and a repository link sat further down its thread.

SemiAnalysis, which benchmarks inference hardware, reported the same result and put it at 56% better performance than the GB200 NVL72 rack. The firm said the figure showed that Google's work to make its TPU software usable outside Google was, in its words, full steam ahead. Neither account has been reproduced elsewhere.

The technique is a single kernel rather than a faster chip. All 92 of Kimi K3's mixture-of-experts layers run in one Pallas kernel, vLLM said, with weight prefetching that reaches across layer boundaries, so transfers for one layer overlap with computation in the previous one.

Neither post gave the batch size, the chip count or the context length behind the numbers, and a tokens-a-second figure depends on all three. Kimi K3's weights are public, which means anyone with the hardware could in principle check the comparison. Nobody outside the two accounts has yet published one.

stories.headline: Anthropic says a 2-week sprint made claude.ai 3.1 times faster
stories.standfirst: Engineers credit a model working in a single Slack channel, and put a fresh web load at 550 milliseconds against 3,085 before the sprint.
body: Anthropic said on Wednesday that a two-week sprint made claude.ai and its desktop app 3.1 times faster, a geometric mean across 13 measurements at the 75th percentile. According to the post, the company compared real user monitoring on 13 August with 27 August, across four journeys it said make up 95% of activity.

A fresh load of claude.ai fell from 3,085 milliseconds to 550, the post said. A desktop cold start went from 6,310 milliseconds to 3,328, loading a conversation on the desktop app from 1,353 to 488, and sending a message in Claude Cowork from 928 milliseconds to 48.

The three authors, Raymond Wang, Sam Attard and Issac G., said the sprint ran in one Slack channel with Claude in every thread. An engineer would open a thread on a slow stretch, Claude would trace it and build a benchmark, then return with pull requests sized for review, anything user-visible behind a flag.

One example: message-tree assembly was resolving the same message ID three times. Cutting that removed 48% of the CPU instructions on the path and 78% of the wall-clock time, the post said, and the team then made any pull request that raised the count fail its tests.

The numbers are Anthropic's own and nobody outside the company has checked them. The post said the work targeted the 75th percentile, and that the 95th percentile, other journeys and the longest conversations may still have room to improve. Anthropic estimates the gains could save tens of thousands of user-hours of waiting a day.

sources.author: Raymond Wang, Sam Attard and Issac G. (Anthropic)

stories.headline: Google ships 2 Gemini 3.8 speech models, says they top Hume benchmark
stories.standfirst: Both models are live in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, and Artificial Analysis puts one of them first on its pronunciation benchmark.
body: Google released two text-to-speech models on Wednesday, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS. Both are live in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. The company says they cover more than 100 languages and dialects, among them Quebec French and Scots English.

Artificial Analysis, which tests models independently, said Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS debuted first on its benchmark for how reliably a model pronounces hard text. It came second on the provider voice arena leaderboard. On a controlled voice arena, Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS took first in Japanese at an Elo of 1,212, with the larger model second.

Google says a user can write a prompt to create a voice, then direct the delivery line by line. It says a voice can be replicated from a 30-second sample after what it describes as consent verification. The library runs from 30 original voices to more than 2,000 production-ready ones, and every clip carries a SynthID watermark, according to the company.

Logan Kilpatrick, who leads Google AI Studio, said on X that the models cost less than the earlier Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS. Google's price list puts audio output for Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS at $9.00 per million tokens through 31 December 2026. Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS is listed at $20.00. The new price rises to $18.00 in January.

Artificial Analysis priced the models per million characters of input text rather than per token, and reached the opposite comparison. It put Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS at $32.98 and the Flash-Lite model at $22.07, against $18.31 for Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS. It measured the larger model at 44.1 characters a second, behind Falcon 2 at 204.9.

stories.headline: OpenAI gives ChatGPT Voice plugins, opens Work tab on phones
stories.standfirst: Voice can now reach a user's email, calendar and Slack, and Plus and Pro subscribers get agentic tasks on mobile.
body: OpenAI said on Tuesday that ChatGPT Voice can now use plugins, including a user's email, calendar and Slack, and that it can be driven by GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna. The company said Voice also works in ChatGPT Work on web and mobile, where it can create documents, decks, sites and spreadsheets.

TechCrunch reported the mobile side separately. Plus and Pro subscribers get the Work tab on their phones for agentic tasks, it said, while Free and Go users can work with plugins and connected apps. The rollout runs on GPT-Live, the conversational model OpenAI put in the desktop app in July, according to the report.

The claims about what Voice can do are OpenAI's own, and nobody outside the company has tested the feature set yet. OpenAI opened its post with "We heard you loud and clear", which reads as a response to complaints that Voice had been cut off from the rest of the product.

Thomas Sottiaux, who works at OpenAI, said he had grown used to calling ChatGPT to check email, do some coding and manage his calendar, and that it works across third-party plugins as well as OpenAI's own. His post had drawn more than 1,100 likes by Tuesday evening.

Conversations can move between devices. A user may start one on a phone and resume it on desktop, TechCrunch said, and voice replies now carry richer text output with a switch between text and speech. OpenAI did not give a date for wider availability.

stories.headline: YouTube lets viewers write their own feeds, built by Gemini
stories.standfirst: Custom feeds turn a typed description into a pinned tab on the home page, and reach web and mobile next month.
body: YouTube said at its Made on YouTube event that viewers will be able to describe the videos they want in their own words and have Google's Gemini build a feed around the description. The feeds appear as tabs pinned to the top of the home page, separate from the main recommendation feed, and roll out on web and mobile from October.

TechCrunch and Wired both reported the feature on Tuesday. A user may ask for "video podcasts to watch during your 30-minute train commute" or "relaxing commentary videos to unwind with", TechCrunch said, and can say what to exclude and what to put first. Users can make more than one feed.

How well it works is not established, and nobody outside YouTube has used it yet. Emily Moxley, YouTube's vice president of product management for viewer AI, put the corpus at more than 20 billion videos and said a viewer is "always one search away from a treasure trove of topics".

The same event brought creator tools. YouTube is adding features to generate ideas and to test thumbnails inside its Studio app, TechCrunch said, alongside an assistant for script analysis and tools aimed at microdramas. The Wall Street Journal framed that set as part of a fight with Netflix over top creators.

Spotify launched its Taste Profile in the United States on the same day, letting Premium subscribers steer their recommendations. Bluesky, Threads, Instagram and X have each offered some form of user-built feed before this.

stories.headline: Enigma message unread since 2005 broken with help from GPT-6 Astra
stories.standfirst: Cryptologic historian Frode Weierud says a German Army signal from July 1941 gave up its key after the model wrote its own Bombe in two days.
body: A German Army Enigma message that had resisted solution since 2005 has been read, according to Frode Weierud of Crypto Cellar Research, who says the cryptanalysis was carried out by OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra under the direction of Carter Leffer. Weierud's account, updated on 19 September, dates the break to 15 September.

The signal, known by its indicator MVUEH, was sent on 10 July 1941. Weierud says the model wrote its own Enigma simulation and Bombe software in Python and C++, then ran the attack using the repeated place name ROSENOW ROSENOW as a crib. It picked message number 172 as the most promising target on its own, he says, and suspected a link to a related message number 173.

The recovered key used wheel order 253, which Weierud notes differs from the other keys known for 10 July. He says the ciphertext also carried transcription errors, and that the left-hand wheel turned over at the 72nd letter, a rare event that complicates a crib attack.

Weierud, who has published Enigma material for decades, writes that what the model achieved in two days "would take a human researcher weeks or even months". That judgement is his own, and the claim rests on his account of the work. Neither OpenAI nor any other cryptanalyst has published an independent reconstruction of the break.

The page reached the front page of Hacker News on Tuesday with 696 points and 408 comments. Messages left unbroken after the wartime archives were opened are a small and well-worked set, and the ones that remain are usually corrupt, short, or both.

stories.headline: Benchmark gives 4 models control of a Corolla, 1 finishes the course
stories.standfirst: Three researchers say they let language models steer a real car around a cone course, and published the token bill for each attempt.
body: A benchmark published at drivingbench.com hands language models direct control of a Toyota Corolla's steering and pedals on a fixed cone course. Of the four models on its leaderboard, only GPT-6 Astra finished. The paper has not verified the runs, and no one else appears to have reproduced them.

The site credits Aditya Ramabadran, Simon Mahns and Tobias Gessler with equal contributions, and describes the work as experimental software with no official affiliation to any car or AI company. Each model gets up to three attempts in one continuous chat, according to the page.

GPT-6 Astra completed the course on its second attempt in 5 minutes 22 seconds, the leaderboard says, after reaching 49% on the first. It puts the best progress of Claude Fable 5.1 at 45%, Grok 4.6 at 11% and GPT-5.6 Sol at 6%.

The finishing run consumed 246.6 million tokens and cost $7.74, according to the same table. Scoring counts how far a model travels along the course centreline while staying within 4 metres of it. Completion time, distance covered, token use and cost also feature.

The page does not say when the runs took place, what prompt or scaffolding each model got, how often it answered, or whether anyone sat in the car. The submission had 67 points and 41 comments on the Hacker News front page an hour after it appeared.

stories.headline: Amazon opens seller tools to outside AI agents, starting with Claude
stories.standfirst: The beta lets United States merchants check inventory, change prices and edit listings from Anthropic's Claude or Amazon's own Quick assistant.
body: Amazon said on Wednesday at its Accelerate seller conference in Seattle that it is opening its seller management tools to third-party AI agents, beginning with Anthropic's Claude and Amazon's own Quick assistant. The beta covers Amazon's United States marketplace, with other countries planned.

A plugin lets sellers check inventory, adjust prices and update listings through either agent, according to GeekWire, which reported from the conference. Amazon says setup takes about 60 seconds and no coding. GeekWire's account does not say how many sellers are in the beta, or which protocol the plugin uses.

Mary Beth Westmoreland, Amazon's vice-president of worldwide selling partner experience, told GeekWire that the aim was that sellers "would never have to log into Seller Central. We would just bring it to them where they work."

Amazon also added a canvas feature to its Seller Assistant for visual analysis of a seller's data, and background automations that watch a business and act once the seller approves. The company says the assistant now keeps a memory of a seller's pricing patterns and growth goals.

More integrations will follow, Amazon says, without naming them. It is also giving primary seller accounts a free 12-month Amazon Quick Plus subscription through 31 December 2026, with two co-workers included at no cost. Anthropic has published nothing of its own on the arrangement.

stories.headline: OpenCode offers free access to Space Bunny, an unnamed stealth coding model
stories.standfirst: The model takes text, images and video, and has a context window of about a million tokens. OpenCode has not said who built it.
body: OpenCode, the open-source coding agent, has added a model called Space Bunny to its Zen and Go model services and made it free to use. Its documentation describes Space Bunny as a stealth model: OpenCode has not named the company that built it. The listing went live on Wednesday.

According to models.dev, the model registry OpenCode uses, Space Bunny is an anonymous preview reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, tool use and multimodal input. It accepts images and video as well as text, and returns text. The listing gives a context window of 1,048,576 tokens, with up to 524,288 tokens of output.

OpenCode says the provider keeps no data and does not use it to train models. Its Go documentation lists usage as unlimited and retention as zero days. Developers select it with the model ID space-bunny-free. The listing sets every price, including cached input, at zero, and marks the weights as closed.

OpenCode describes the free access as available for a limited time. A public tracker of free AI offers lists it as ending on 30 September. OpenCode merged the change into its code on Wednesday. Nobody has published benchmark results, and nobody outside OpenCode has yet reported testing the model or identifying its maker.

stories.headline: Nvidia releases 100M open-weight diarization model, says it tops VoiceArena
stories.standfirst: Nemotron 3 Diarization labels who spoke when for up to 8 speakers, and Nvidia says it cuts diarization error to 14.72% against 19.3% for the next system.
body: Nvidia released Nemotron 3 Diarization on Wednesday, a 100-million-parameter open-weight model that labels which speaker is talking in a recording or a live stream, for up to 8 speakers. The company published it in a post on Hugging Face.

Nvidia says the model ranks first on VoiceArena's Diarization-Bench, with a 14.72% diarization error rate against 19.3% for the next system. That figure is the company's own, taken from its post, and nobody else has yet published a test of the release.

The model takes single-channel audio at 16 kHz and runs offline or streaming, with input-buffer latency configurable from 30.4 seconds down to 0.32 seconds, according to the post. It carries the OpenMDW License Agreement v1.1 rather than one of the usual open-source licences.

Nvidia puts the gain at an average 40% relative reduction in diarization error at 1.04 seconds of latency, measured against its own earlier Streaming Sortformer baseline. On DIHARD III it reports 12.73% error at the 30.4-second setting. Both comparisons are the company's, on datasets it selected.

The weights sit on Hugging Face and the code ships in Nvidia's NeMo Speech framework on GitHub, with a demo Space linked from the post. The model page returned an authorisation error to an anonymous request, which may mean the licence gates access to the files.

stories.headline: Benchmark scores 76 decision systems, puts TypeSafe's Jev on top
stories.standfirst: JevBench, published by Benchmark Heaven under an MIT licence, ranks typed decision models on 534 public and 308 sealed decisions, and its authors call the set partial.
body: Benchmark Heaven published version 1.4.0 of JevBench on Wednesday, a leaderboard that scores 76 typed decision systems on 534 public and 308 sealed decisions. Such systems take a state and a bounded rubric and return a typed answer rather than free text, according to the benchmark's own description.

The leaderboard puts TypeSafe AI's Jev 1.13.0 first on 63.3, followed by JevK5 v0.2.0 on 62.0, Hopper on 59.4, Winnow-12B Q8 on 55.6 and reflex 4B on 54.0. The score weighs accuracy above chance against calibration, then applies separate gates for speed and cost, according to the benchmark's own methodology page.

The run places two models this paper reported on Monday, when community benchmarks disagreed over which was faster. Convai Innovations' open-source Laya sits 32nd on 30.3. An OpenJev entry, credited to razorback16 rather than to the checkpoints trending on Hugging Face, sits 21st on 36.9.

A third of the decisions are held back. The page says the text and answers of the 308 sealed items stay private and only system-level aggregates appear, and that a penalty applies when a system's public accuracy exceeds its sealed accuracy by more than 25 points. The harness, the public tasks and the scoring rules are on GitHub under an MIT licence.

Commenters on Hacker News, where the Show HN post drew 123 points and 33 comments, questioned what the tasks cover. One, hbrn, wrote that Jev performs on a par with a system built in a couple of days and costs twice as much. Another said the tasks do not cover much of what Jev was likely trained to do.

The author, posting as florianstandhar, said a missing zero-shot baseline, BART-large-MNLI, would be added in the next run, and invited submissions through the repository. The benchmark's own page says its scores describe the tested configurations rather than every application.

stories.headline: Spotify launches Taste Profile in US, lets Premium users steer recommendations
stories.standfirst: TechCrunch reported the beta feature shows listeners how Spotify reads their taste and lets them change it in plain language, for subscribers aged 18 and over.
body: Spotify began rolling out Taste Profile to Premium subscribers in the United States on Wednesday, a beta feature that shows listeners how the service reads their taste and lets them change it in plain language, TechCrunch reported.

That report is the only account of the US launch so far. No statement from Spotify appears in it, and the company gave no timeline for reaching a wider audience, according to TechCrunch. The feature had run in beta in New Zealand before this.

The profile covers podcasts and audiobooks as well as music. TechCrunch said listeners can ask for more variety, raise or lower particular genres and artists, and keep things like sleep sounds or children's music from shaping what Spotify serves them.

Spotify's co-chief executive Gustav Soderstrom showed the feature at SXSW in March, according to TechCrunch. It remains a beta in the United States, where only Premium subscribers aged 18 and over can use it for now.

stories.headline: OpenAI gives Ukraine its Daybreak cyber defence system and GPT-5.6 Sol
stories.standfirst: The company says the tools will help protect hospitals and power plants from attack. A defence researcher told the BBC that Ukraine already uses AI tools from Google.
body: OpenAI will give the government of Ukraine access to Daybreak, its AI cyber defence system, the company said on Wednesday. The aim is to help protect civilian infrastructure such as hospitals and power plants. The BBC reported that the arrangement is free of charge. It includes access to GPT-5.6 Sol, which the broadcaster described as a rival to Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models.

According to the BBC, Daybreak can quickly identify weaknesses in digital systems and help develop fixes. OpenAI has not published figures on how well it performs, so that description rests on the company's own account. Ukraine's national cyber incident team, CERT-UA, recorded nearly 6,000 attacks in 2025, the broadcaster said.

George Osborne, the former UK chancellor who now heads OpenAI for Countries, said civilian infrastructure must be defended against both physical and digital attacks. Rafe Pilling of the security firm Sophos told the BBC that Russian cyber operations had been a key part of the Kremlin's aggression against Ukraine since 2014. He said the tools could act as a force multiplier.

Jamie MacColl, a cyber researcher at the Royal United Services Institute, said Western technology firms may gain valuable data and intelligence from an active conflict. He noted that Ukraine already has AI tools from OpenAI's competitors, including Google. Neither OpenAI nor the BBC gave a start date or said how long the arrangement will last.

stories.headline: Unreal Labs open-sources agent harness, claims 40% saving against Codex
stories.standfirst: Unreal Agent runs tool calls asynchronously so the model no longer pays tokens to wait, according to the company's benchmark post.
body: Unreal Labs has released Unreal Agent, an open-source agent harness written in Go, and says it cuts the cost of running coding agents by handling tool calls asynchronously. The company says the design "relieves the underlying model of the need to manage waits, polls, and heartbeats for tools", which lets calls run in parallel without spending tokens on the bookkeeping.

The company reports up to 40% lower cost than Codex on what it describes as production workloads. Its own runs put the harness at 57.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at a total cost of $1,428, 65.8% on SWE-Atlas at $936, and 72.4% on DeepSWE 1.1 at $1,367. On ALE-CLI it reports a 30% full pass rate at $217.

The release on GitHub includes a Go library, a runner executable and the benchmark runner itself, which would let others reproduce the figures. All of the numbers above come from Unreal Labs, and no outside party has checked them.

The post, dated 22 September, reached the Hacker News front page on Tuesday with 217 points and 114 comments. Unreal Labs publishes the code at github.com/unreallabsai/unreal-agent, and says its founders previously worked at CERN and DeepMind.

stories.headline: Developer says Claude Code skips AGENTS.md when telemetry is off
stories.standfirst: Przemek Szypowicz reports the loader sits behind a remote feature flag that fails closed, and says users get no warning when the file is ignored.
body: A developer says recent builds of Anthropic's Claude Code quietly stop reading local AGENTS.md files when telemetry is switched off. Przemek Szypowicz, writing on his own blog on Wednesday, says the behaviour appears in version 2.1.277 and later, and that he tested it on 2.1.280.

His method was a canary. Szypowicz says he created an empty directory containing only an AGENTS.md file with the word PERIWINKLE in it, then asked the tool for the canary word with telemetry disabled. He says the file was not read when DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 was set.

The cause, according to the post, is that the agents-md plugin ships with isOnByDefault set to false and checks a remote flag named tengu_agents_md_mod, falling back to unavailable when it cannot reach the service.

Szypowicz says that makes the loader fail closed for anyone who has turned off nonessential traffic, and that users on third-party gateways such as Bedrock and Vertex may be affected. He suggests a one-line CLAUDE.md containing @AGENTS.md as a workaround.

Anthropic has not responded publicly to the post, and the paper has not reproduced the test. Szypowicz presents the findings as his own observations rather than confirmed behaviour. The post reached the Hacker News front page on Wednesday with 178 points and 67 comments.

stories.headline: Microsoft seizes 50 sites behind phishing kit that took 12,000 inboxes
stories.standfirst: Microsoft said EvilTokens sold device-code phishing for $1,500 and a $500 monthly fee, and that about 1,000 criminals used it before the takedown.
body: Microsoft said it disrupted EvilTokens, a phishing service that compromised more than 12,000 email inboxes at over 10,000 organisations worldwide. Acting on a 15 September order from the US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, the company and its partners seized 50 websites and disabled more than 175 domains, CyberScoop reported.

Ars Technica described EvilTokens as an end-to-end platform that makes mass compromises faster and easier. Microsoft said the service emerged in February 2026, and CyberScoop reported that about 1,000 criminals used it between then and June. Its operators charged $1,500 to buy in and $500 a month after that, according to Microsoft.

Microsoft said the kit sold AI features alongside the phishing. Assistants tailored lures and sifted through stolen mailboxes to pick out high-value targets, and the platform carried 44 email themes for building templates and landing pages. The description is Microsoft's own.

Health-ISAC, Cloudflare, OpenAI, Shadowserver, TRM Labs, SpyCloud and Coinbase joined the disruption, CyberScoop reported. UK Metropolitan Police arrested two men on 18 September in greater London on suspicion of making articles for use in fraud and money laundering. Police released both on bail.

Steven Masada, Microsoft's associate general counsel, said the takedown removed the infrastructure but not the model it demonstrated. Microsoft correlated at least 13 complaints to the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center with the service, worth about $1.7 million in reported losses. Coinbase traced about $1.1 million in revenue to the operators, according to CyberScoop.

stories.headline: Altworld releases 27B writing model, says it beats GPT-6 Astra on messages
stories.standfirst: Hemmingway-1 is a fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B aimed at everyday email and chat, and it is the ninth most trending model on Hugging Face.
body: A small outfit called Altworld has published Hemmingway-1, a 27-billion-parameter model built on Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B and tuned for everyday writing such as messages and email. The model card says it "writes the best everyday messages of any model we tested", and claims it outperforms larger models including GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 on communication tasks.

The weights carry a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence, which allows non-commercial use, with commercial terms available by agreement. The model page had 539 likes and 3,787 downloads on Wednesday, putting it ninth on Hugging Face's trending list. It was first published on 20 September and last updated on 22 September.

Most of the numbers on the card are Altworld's own. It reports 72% on what it calls difficult persuasive writing against 9% for GPT-6 Astra, and says the model finished "twenty-six points clear of the next model" on human-likeness. The card states plainly that CommunicationBench, Human-Likeness and StoryBench are the company's own benchmarks.

The one external figure Altworld cites is a third place on EQ-Bench 4, an independent emotional-intelligence benchmark it did not build. No other party appears to have run Hemmingway-1 against the models it names, so the comparative claims rest on Altworld's testing alone.

stories.headline: Alibaba launches Qwen Intelligence, says its 3 phone agents run on Honor
stories.standfirst: The company put end-to-end task completion at 90% and said its planner agent tops MobilePA-Bench, a benchmark suite Alibaba wrote and published itself.
body: Alibaba launched Qwen Intelligence on Wednesday, a package of three agents it is selling to phone makers. The three are a planner agent, a mobile-use agent that drives apps, and a creative agent that makes images. Trade reports of the launch say the stack is already running on Honor's MagicOS.

The planner agent takes first place on MobilePA-Bench, according to Alibaba, which published that benchmark alongside the launch. A technical report for Qwen-Planner-Agent 27B puts the model at 77.05% overall on it, 9.83 points above its baseline, at an estimated $2.41 per 1,000 tasks.

Alibaba put the mobile-use agent at 82.1 on MobileWorld, 92.2 on MobileWorld-Real and 97.2 on AndroidDaily, with a 90% end-to-end success rate. It said the agent calls an app's interface where one exists and falls back to reading the screen and tapping where none does.

Every figure here is Alibaba's, measured on tests it chose, and the benchmark its planner leads is one it wrote. No outside evaluator has published a score for any of the three agents. Alibaba did not give pricing for phone makers, or name other handset brands.

The creative agent produces a first image in about three seconds, which Alibaba said is roughly twice as fast as leading peers. It did not name the peers or the hardware. Honor has published no figures of its own, and the companies did not say how many phones carry the stack.

stories.headline: Qualcomm to buy PickNik Robotics, says MoveIt stays open source
stories.standfirst: The company said it will keep MoveIt 1 and 2 under their existing licence and fold PickNik's commercial MoveIt Pro into its Dragonwing platform. Terms were not disclosed.
body: Qualcomm has agreed to acquire PickNik, the Boulder company that maintains the open-source robotics framework MoveIt, the two said at ROSCon in Toronto. Terms were not disclosed, and the deal is subject to customary closing conditions.

Three market-news accounts carried the announcement within an hour of each other on Wednesday, and The Robot Report published the fullest account of it. Qualcomm said it will keep MoveIt 1 and 2 open source under their existing licence and community roadmaps, and will continue supporting MoveIt on third-party hardware.

MoveIt handles motion planning and manipulation, the software that decides how a robot arm moves. Qualcomm said pairing it with Dragonwing, its robotics chip platform, should shorten the path from an AI model to planning and real-time control. That claim is the company's own.

PickNik was founded in 2015 and counted Google as an early customer. Dave Coleman, its founder and chief product officer, said joining Qualcomm would let the company expand investment in MoveIt as a training platform for robotics. Nakul Duggal, a Qualcomm executive vice-president, said PickNik had earned trust through its stewardship of MoveIt.

Neither company gave a price, a closing date or a headcount. Nvidia released Isaac ROS 5.0 as free and open source at the same conference a day earlier. Qualcomm has not said what happens to MoveIt's governance once the deal closes.

stories.headline: UK regulator would put AI assistants on Google's choice screens
stories.standfirst: The Competition and Markets Authority proposed that assistants meeting Google's technical and security criteria sit alongside search engines, with consultation open until 9 October.
body: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority proposed on Wednesday that Google show Android and Chrome users a choice of search providers on first setup, and that AI assistants be allowed onto those screens. Assistants that meet Google's technical and security criteria could sit alongside search engines under the proposals.

The proposals would also prompt users once a year to pick a default, and would require search providers to attribute publisher content so readers can reach the source material. Reuters and Engadget both reported the package on Wednesday.

Sarah Cardell, the authority's chief executive, said the way people search for information online is changing. She said the regulator was responding to the rise of AI assistants, which people increasingly use as a search service but which Google's choice screens do not carry.

Assistants would have to meet Google's own technical and security criteria to appear on the screens. Reuters named ChatGPT and Perplexity as examples of the services at issue. The authority has not said how it would test whether Google applies those criteria fairly.

Consultation runs until 9 October, and the authority is expected to make a final decision by the end of the year. Neither account says when any requirement would take effect. Google's response is not in either report, and the company has not published one.

stories.headline: Developers fill X with games they say Opus 5.5 built in one prompt
stories.standfirst: A Roblox fighter, browser Minecraft clones and a guitar-shop simulator drew thousands of likes within a day, though two builders said their demos are unfinished.
body: Developers spent Tuesday and Wednesday posting games and 3D scenes they said Claude Opus 5.5 produced from a single prompt, a day after Anthropic released the model. The most widely shared came from the account WoahWurdz, which posted a Roblox fighting game in the style of Super Smash Bros and passed 2,600 likes.

WoahWurdz called it one-shotted, said it was built only using toolbox and nothing else, and put it leagues above Fable. Three hours later the same account said the one-shot prompt was still not finished and that it would post a finished result once it was. What circulated, on the account's own description, is a partial run.

The second most-shared build carries its own qualification. bijanbowen posted a guitar-shop simulator that turns into a beat-em-up when the player makes too much noise, and said the model produced more than 300 individual guitar models with every instrument playable. The same post called it a bit laggy in three.js and said it would be redone in Blender or Godot.

Browser Minecraft clones were the other common test. buildwithsid posted one running in a browser that passed 900 likes. luckeyfaraday said Opus 5.5 gave the best result they had seen on a one-shot HTML Minecraft test they run against every major model, from one prompt into one file with no iteration, and placed it ahead of GPT-6 Astra.

Not all of the work is games. Voxyz_ai posted an animation and said the model wrote the story, drew every frame in JavaScript with no image assets, synthesised the music in Python, then went through the render second by second. gpumaxxer said a 20-hour overnight run built an Unreal Engine world of agents told to form a society, and that by morning the agents were fighting.

Every claim here is the builder's own, attached to a video rather than to code. None of the demos has been reproduced by anyone else, a clip does not show how many attempts came before it, and two of the most-shared builders have already said theirs is unfinished or needs rebuilding. What the posts establish is enthusiasm and volume, not a measured capability.

stories.headline: Engineer says Opus 5.5 wrote a GPU kernel at 35.5 times PyTorch
stories.standfirst: Elliot Arledge published a run-by-run comparison on his own hardware and put GPT-6 Astra second at 24.8 times the baseline.
body: A performance engineer said Claude Opus 5.5 wrote a GPU kernel that ran 35.5 times faster than an optimised PyTorch baseline on the KernelBench-Mega benchmark, against 24.8 times for GPT-6 Astra. Elliot Arledge posted the result on Wednesday, describing the output as a Kimi-Linear decode megakernel.

Arledge said he gave each model one session on his own RTX PRO 6000 machine, with no budget cap. The figures are isolated regrades, he said, made after an audit of the run traces and submissions for reward hacking. That check matters: a kernel benchmark can be gamed by a model that weakens the baseline it is timed against.

The runs differed more in shape than in their final numbers. Arledge said Opus 5.5 had a working megakernel at 21 times the baseline after 31 minutes. Astra reached 14 times after an hour, then spent four hours moving from 24 to 25. Fable 5.1 reached 23 times in two hours before the session died on an API error.

One session per model is a small sample and the traces are not published, so the ordering may not hold on a rerun. Arledge said he runs 20 such jobs in parallel. That is why he values how the model reports status: he said it takes him seconds to see what is blocking a run. He also said he suspects reports of weakened kernel performance apply to TPU or Trainium rather than CUDA.

A week of testing at Every produced a more mixed account. The publication said Opus 5.5 will not stop on its own and will eat a weekly limit. Given ten minutes to produce a run of show, it built a data generator and handouts, then ran out of time before the schedule. It also rejected 90% of its own work for reasons its designer could not trace.

Every also said the model builds on feedback instead of arguing with it. Its prose is the most readable the publication has measured, it said, though it still buries the lede. On cost, the account SahilExec ran the same prompt through the same harness. It logged $75 and 2 hours 10 minutes for Opus 5.5, against $61 and 1 hour 25 minutes for Astra.

stories.headline: Sanders bill would ban superintelligence, create Department of AI
stories.standfirst: The Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act would pause advanced AI work until a new federal regulator writes safety rules, and carries prison terms of up to 20 years.
body: Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar presented legislation on Wednesday that would permanently ban artificial superintelligence and create a cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence. The bill would also pause advanced AI development until the new regulator writes safety rules, and would require federal approval before an advanced system is deployed.

The Associated Press reported the introduction, which follows a September 3 announcement from Sanders's office that the two intended to bring the bill forward. That release defines superintelligence as a system that surpasses human intelligence or could overthrow human governments. The AP renders the same definition as exceeding human cognitive ability or planning humanity's destruction.

Penalties run to 20 years in prison in some cases, a term Sanders's office compares to unlawfully developing nuclear weapons. The release also describes a corporate death penalty for entities that break the ban, and an AI Advisory Board to supply scientific guidance to the new department.

Employees at two of the companies the bill would cover have endorsed it, according to the AP. They include Juan Felipe Cerón Uribe, a researcher on OpenAI's Safety Systems team, and Swante Scholz, a software engineer at Google DeepMind, who said the current path leads to what he called an existential catastrophe for humanity.

"It doesn't take a genius to say, 'slow it down,'" Sanders said. The bill faces long odds in a Republican-controlled Congress that has not agreed on narrower AI rules, and President Trump has resisted regulation. The AP account carries no response from OpenAI or Google DeepMind, and the measure may not reach a vote.

stories.headline: Tekever closes first tranche of 500 million euro round at 5.5 billion value
stories.standfirst: The Portuguese drone maker is hunting acquisitions after the first close, and its chief executive said a listing is on the horizon.
body: Tekever, a Portuguese maker of surveillance drones, has completed the first close of a funding round targeting €500 million, or about $580 million, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. The round values the company at €5.5 billion, roughly five times the €1.2 billion it reached in May last year.

Chief executive Ricardo Mendes said the money is meant to fund acquisitions as well as internal development. "The fund raise is precisely designed to support that growth, not only organically, developing new technology, but through acquisitions," he said. The company is raising from both new and existing backers.

Mendes also said the defence technology market will go through what he called tremendous consolidation in coming years, and that an initial public offering is "on our horizon". He gave no timetable, and the phrase commits Tekever to nothing.

The two accounts of the round use different currencies. Bloomberg gives the €5.5 billion valuation and the €500 million target. CNBC put the valuation at $6.4 billion, which is the euro figure converted. Neither account names the investors in the first close, nor says how much of the €500 million it raised.

CNBC tied the valuation to defence spending driven by the war in Ukraine. Neither account gives Tekever's revenue. A first close is not a completed round, and the rest of the €500 million may not be raised on these terms, or at all.

stories.headline: Samsung says it validated 16GB LPDDR6 on Qualcomm's next flagship chip
stories.standfirst: The memory ran at 10.7 gigabits per second on Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, Seoul Economic Daily said, citing industry sources.
body: Samsung has validated a 16-gigabyte LPDDR6 memory package running at 10.7 gigabits per second on Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, Seoul Economic Daily reported on Wednesday, citing industry sources. Validation on the application processor is the last step before phone makers can ship the memory.

Samsung's own figures for LPDDR6 put the bandwidth gain at up to 45% over LPDDR5X and power efficiency at up to 21% better. Both are the company's numbers. The paper quotes a Samsung vice-president saying it would supply the memory in time to match customers' commercialisation schedules.

Two forms of the bandwidth claim are in circulation. Seoul Economic Daily reports Samsung supporting up to 125 gigabits per second. Other accounts of the same validation give 114 gigabytes per second. The units differ by a factor of eight and no account reconciles them, so the throughput figure remains unsettled.

Neither Samsung nor Qualcomm has named a phone. The report says commercialisation is within reach and that expansion is expected to start next year. Coverage has linked the part to Samsung's next Galaxy flagship, but the validation notice itself does not mention a handset.

Qualcomm announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 this week and said its top chip can run a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model on the device. Running a model of that size locally depends on how much memory the phone carries and how fast it can be read.

stories.headline: Alibaba releases 5 Qwen audio models, cuts speech recognition price
stories.standfirst: Qwen said the upgrade covers recognition, synthesis and realtime conversation, adds two models, and cuts prices by up to 95%.
body: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen-Audio-3.1 on Wednesday, an upgrade covering speech recognition, text-to-speech and realtime conversation, with two models added. Qwen said prices fall across the line: text-to-speech by about 70%, realtime by about 85%, and speech recognition by up to 95%.

The pricing is the company's own. Qwen Cloud lists the ASR Flash file-transcription model at $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.47 per million output tokens, with a rate limit of 600 requests a minute. The announcement gives the percentage cuts without the prior prices behind them.

The two new models are ASR-Next and TTS-Next. Qwen said ASR-Next handles multi-speaker recognition with speaker labels and timestamps, and can caption ambient and machine sounds. It said TTS-Next combines a language model with diffusion to generate voice, sound effects and background audio in a single pass.

Qwen said the existing recognition model gained multilingual and dialect coverage and a polishing step that strips fillers and repetitions from transcripts, and that a user can interrupt the realtime model mid-turn. No independent benchmark has tested any of these claims in this material.

Qwen also said the realtime model slows down and responds empathetically when it senses a low mood. The announcement does not say what triggers that behaviour or how the company measures it. The company said more APIs are coming, and pointed to Qwen Cloud listings for the recognition and realtime models.

stories.headline: Firmus in talks over $10 billion for Indonesian data centre, Bloomberg says
stories.standfirst: The Australian company is negotiating with lenders on a financing deal to buy Nvidia chips, Bloomberg reported. Firmus has not commented publicly.
body: Firmus Technologies is in talks with lenders over a financing deal worth roughly $10 billion to buy Nvidia chips for its data centre in Indonesia, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. The report describes talks rather than a signed agreement, and names no lender.

Two market wire accounts carried the report within the hour and described the company differently. FirstSquawk called Firmus "Nvidia-supported" and said it aims to raise the money "for AI chip development". financialjuice called the company "Nvidia-backed". Bloomberg's own wording says only that the financing would buy Nvidia chips.

The distinction matters and no account resolves it. A company buying Nvidia parts and a company Nvidia has invested in are different things, and the two wire posts assert the second without pointing to a stake or a figure. Nvidia has not said anything about Firmus in this material.

None of the three accounts gives terms, a closing date, or how much of the $10 billion would go on chips rather than on the site. Firmus did not comment in any of them, and the reporting rests on Bloomberg alone. The deal may not close on the terms described, or at all.

stories.headline: Samsung renames next DRAM node around wafer bonding, ZDNet Korea says
stories.standfirst: D0a now refers to the B1b hybrid-bonding process, while the vertical-transistor design that carried the name becomes D0a-V, according to the report.
body: Samsung Electronics has moved B1b, a wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding process, onto its official DRAM roadmap and given it the D0a designation, ZDNet Korea reported on Wednesday. B1b had been in research and development outside the roadmap until the revision.

Two accounts carried the reporting. jukan05 posted a full translation of the article, and SemiconductorsX summarised it and quoted the same unnamed source. Both trace to ZDNet Korea, which attributes the change to people close to the plan. Samsung has not published anything on the revision.

D0a is meant to be Samsung's first DRAM below 10 nanometres. The most recent part in volume is 1c, around 11 to 12 nanometres, with 1d at 10 to 11 and likely the last of the class, according to the report, which notes these are marketing terms rather than physical dimensions.

B1b builds the memory cells on one wafer and the driver circuitry on another, then joins them by connecting their copper interconnects directly. Vertical-channel DRAM, now labelled D0a-V, takes a different route, cutting cell area from 6F² to 4F², but it needs high-aspect-ratio etching and new materials to hold down leakage.

Samsung is reviewing B1b for HBM5, which the report expects in mass production around 2029 with a target of 50% or more over HBM4E on operating speed. Commercialisation of B1b-based D0a is at least two years out, and the industry expects the investment schedule around the middle of next year, the report said.

stories.headline: China surveys Broadcom switch use in state data centres, FT says
stories.standfirst: Beijing's state-assets regulator counted the switches in state-controlled facilities and could issue informal guidance to cut their use, according to the Financial Times.
body: China's State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission has surveyed the number of Broadcom switches running in state-backed data centres, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday. The newspaper tied the survey to a campaign to move state computing onto domestic parts.

Reuters and Techmeme both carried the report on Wednesday without adding independent confirmation, and the paper has seen no comment from Broadcom or from the commission. The Financial Times said preliminary findings put Broadcom switches at as much as 90% of the equipment in use, a share no other outlet has published.

On those findings the commission may issue informal guidance telling state-run data centres to scale back their use of the switches, the Financial Times said. Informal guidance is not a ban. The report did not give a timetable, name the facilities covered, or say how many sites the survey reached.

Nvidia products are already barred from state-backed data centres, according to the report, which leaves switches among the last large categories of American hardware still widely installed in them. The material available carries no figure for Broadcom's revenue from Chinese state buyers, and the 90% share describes equipment counted, not money.

Two accounts summarising the report on X framed it as part of a push for full-stack hardware independence in China. That framing is theirs. The Financial Times report, as relayed, describes a survey and possible guidance, not a decision to pull the switches out.

stories.headline: Vals AI puts GPT-6 Sol 8th on its index at half the cost
stories.standfirst: The evaluator said the model scores about level with GPT-5.6 Sol while OpenAI has halved its per-token price, and that it slips on finance, tax and law.
body: Vals AI said GPT-6 Sol ranks 8th on the Vals Index, about level with GPT-5.6 Sol at half the cost. The evaluator posted the results on Wednesday, a day after OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. It gave no overall index score in the posts.

The figures are the evaluator's own, from runs it conducted, and the paper has not reproduced them. Vals AI said it ran the model on OpenAI's default provider settings, leaving temperature, top-p and top-k at their defaults and setting reasoning effort to maximum.

The gains are in code. Vals AI put GPT-6 Sol 7 points above GPT-5.6 Sol on its Vibe Code test and 5 points above on Code Migration. It said the model regresses on several of its knowledge-work benchmarks, among them finance, tax and law, which it said reward completeness of answer.

On BioMysteryBench, an open-source benchmark for agentic biology tasks, Vals AI placed GPT-6 Sol 4th at 74.8%, behind three models tied at 79.3%. It put the cost at $0.66 per test and called that cost-effective. The evaluator did not name the three models above it.

Vals AI gave the context window as 1 million tokens and maximum output as 128,000. It said OpenAI has cut per-token pricing by half, from $4 and $20 per million to $2 and $10. Vals AI has not published the task mix behind the index, so the ranking may not hold on a particular workload.

stories.headline: Taiwan export orders reach $102.96 billion in August, ministry says
stories.standfirst: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs put August export orders 71.4 percent above a year earlier, the first month above $100 billion.
body: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs said August export orders came to $102.96 billion, 71.4 percent above the same month a year earlier. The figure is the first monthly total above $100 billion, and passes the previous record of $97.94 billion set in July.

Taiwan's Central News Agency reported the ministry's numbers and attributed the rise to demand for AI servers and to work by large US cloud providers on their own application-specific chips. The Commercial Times carried the same figures, according to the account SemiconductorsX, which posted them on Wednesday.

Electronics orders came to $45.75 billion, up 83.9 percent, and information and communication products to $34.21 billion, up 100.5 percent, the agency reported. The two categories together account for about 78 percent of the month's orders. The ministry did not break either total down by customer.

The ministry forecast September orders of $106.0 billion to $109.1 billion, a range it put at 50.7 to 55.1 percent above a year earlier, and said the full year could reach $1.1 trillion against $743.73 billion in 2025. Export orders record demand booked rather than goods shipped, and may not convert in the same month.

stories.headline: Carnegie report traces 57% of elite AI researchers to Chinese degrees
stories.standfirst: The share of top AI researchers who took an undergraduate degree in China rose from 27 percent in 2022, the report says.
body: A report published this week by Carnegie China said 57 percent of the world's elite AI researchers took their undergraduate degree in China in 2025, against 27 percent in 2022. The share holding a US undergraduate degree fell from 46 percent to 13 percent over the same three years.

The report is the work of Damien Ma and Binyi Yang. Two accounts circulated the figures on Wednesday. The researcher Kyle Chan linked the report itself. The account teortaxesTex posted a different pair of numbers, giving the 2022 Chinese share as 46 percent and the US share as 20 percent. The report's own figures are 27 and 46.

Where researchers trained and where they work are separate counts. The report put 41 percent of AI researchers working in the United States in 2025 against 34 percent in China, and said Chinese retention rose from 57 percent in 2022 to 69 percent in 2025. US retention was 89 percent.

The flow still runs one way, the report said, counting 30 China-origin researchers working in the United States for every one US-origin researcher working in China. Origin here means the country of a researcher's undergraduate degree, a proxy that may not match nationality or where someone grew up.

The report also gives a net US gain of 2,145 researchers in 2025 and a net Chinese loss of 1,729. It sets those counts beside the rising Chinese retention figure without reconciling the two in its summary, and does not say how the researcher sample was drawn.

stories.headline: Anthropic in talks for 1 gigawatt of Apollo-backed compute, report says
stories.standfirst: The Information reported early talks to lease capacity from Stream, a data centre developer majority-owned by Apollo Global Management.
body: Anthropic is in early talks to lease up to a gigawatt of compute capacity from Stream, a data centre developer majority-owned by Apollo Global Management, The Information reported this week. Neither company has announced an agreement, and the report describes the talks as early.

The story carries the byline of Amir Efrati, who posted it on Wednesday, and the account rohanpaul_ai summarised it the same day. Both trace to the same outlet. The talks rest on that single report, and no party to them has confirmed the capacity figure in public.

Apollo said in 2025 that Stream controlled more than 4 gigawatts of powered land, according to the report. Anthropic could fill the sites with Google TPUs co-designed with Broadcom, the report said, and Nvidia GPUs are also under discussion.

A direct lease would move Anthropic past part of the cloud-provider layer it has used to date. That could give the company more say over chip supply, hardware configuration and cost, the report said, while shifting more of the financing and the operating work onto Anthropic itself.

Neither account gives a figure for what the lease would cost or when the two sides might sign. The report describes the gigawatt as an upper bound on what the talks cover rather than a contracted amount, and does not say how much of Stream's land it would take up.

stories.headline: Alibaba to open first cloud regions in Turkey, Finland and Netherlands
stories.standfirst: Bloomberg reported the three sites will open within 12 months, as part of a global buildout Alibaba puts at 20 gigawatts.
body: Alibaba said it plans to open its first cloud regions in Turkey, Finland and the Netherlands over the next 12 months, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. The company is adding data centre capacity in the Middle East as well, according to the same report.

Bloomberg's account was carried the same day by Techmeme and by Bloomberg's own account on X, both pointing at the one story. No second publication has the plan, so the country list and the timing rest on a single outlet's reporting.

The 20-gigawatt figure is Alibaba's own and describes a global buildout rather than the three new regions. It may include capacity already running. Bloomberg gave no capacity figure for Turkey, Finland or the Netherlands, and no cost for the three sites.

Bloomberg set the expansion against competition between China and the United States in AI chips and models. That framing is the outlet's rather than a statement from Alibaba, and the report does not say the new regions answer any particular US measure. A cloud region is a company's own unit of account and may cover more than one building.

stories.headline: Vals AI puts Xiaomi's MiMo v2.6 Pro and Flash top of open-weight index
stories.standfirst: The evaluator priced the two models at $0.39 and $0.20 per task, against $6.47 for Kimi K3, and said both sit on its cost frontier.
body: Vals AI said Xiaomi's MiMo V2.6 Pro and Flash are the new first and second open-weight models on the Vals Index. The evaluator posted the results early on Wednesday, a day after Xiaomi released the two models. It put the gain over their predecessor, MiMo v2.5, at 19 to 20 points on the index score.

The figures are the evaluator's own, from runs it conducted, and the paper has not reproduced them. Vals AI said Flash costs $0.20 per task and Pro $0.39, and that both score higher than Kimi K3 at $6.47 and GLM 5.3 at $6.73. That puts the cost gap at 17 to 34 times, according to its posts.

Vals AI put the two models within 0.04 points of each other overall, at 59.73 and 59.69. The order in which it gave those figures would place Flash above Pro, which does not sit easily with ranking Pro first. The evaluator did not say which score belongs to which model.

Pro is better at finance, Vibe Code Bench, Code Migration and Legal Research, Vals AI said, and Flash better at Terminal-Bench and EMB. It called Flash the better terminal-agent model at half the price. Both score under 45 on Code Migration, where the evaluator put the frontier at 55 to 68.

The models were run on Xiaomi's default provider settings, at temperature 1 and top-p 0.95, Vals AI said. It gave the context window as 1 million tokens and maximum output as 128,000. Neither Xiaomi nor Vals AI has published the task mix behind the index, so the ordering may not hold on a particular workload.

stories.headline: Microsoft plans Copilot discounts of up to 50%, The Information says
stories.standfirst: Four market accounts relayed the report within minutes of each other on Tuesday, and they differ on the size of the cut.
body: Microsoft is preparing discounts of 30% to 50% on corporate Copilot subscriptions, The Information reported on Tuesday. The outlet tied the cuts to a new Copilot "super app" that brings coding tools and AI agents together, according to accounts relaying the report.

The relays do not agree on the figure. Wall St Engine put the range at 30% to 50%. StockSavvyShay put it at about 40% and said it applies to large enterprise customers. First Squawk and Financial Juice carried the headline without a number.

All four accounts rest on the same report, and none of them cites the article's detail. Microsoft has not commented on the pricing, and the paper has not seen The Information's piece. No start date for the discounts appears in any of the summaries.

The Information separately reported that software companies are cutting prices to drive AI adoption, with longer free trials, more AI credits and straight discounts. That piece is about the sector rather than Microsoft, and the outlet did not link the two.

stories.headline: Artificial Analysis puts Opus 5.5 at $5.98 per task, near Opus 5
stories.standfirst: The evaluator said a 20% price cut and cheaper cache reads offset a token-usage increase that would otherwise have pushed the figure to $10.51.
body: Artificial Analysis said Claude Opus 5.5 costs $5.98 to run its Intelligence Index, against $5.86 for Opus 5, both at maximum reasoning. The evaluator published the figures on Tuesday, hours after Anthropic released the model. It said the two are similar.

Getting there took two price cuts against one increase, Artificial Analysis said. Opus 5.5 uses more tokens than Opus 5, which on its own would have raised cost per task by about 80%, to $10.51. Anthropic's 20% cut to base prices brought that to $8.41.

Cutting cache reads to $0.20 per million tokens took a further 29% off, the evaluator said, landing at $5.98. The 29% is a further cut on top of the base-price reduction, not a restatement of it. PhotonCap put the cache-read cut at 60% against Opus 5, according to its summary of Anthropic's announcement.

On OpenAI's side, Artificial Analysis said GPT-6 Sol and Luna halve the cost of the models they replace while scoring about the same on its index. It put the driver at a roughly 50% reduction in token pricing rather than any change in how much the models write.

Simon Willison, who writes about language models, said GPT-6 Luna is half the price of GPT-5.6 Luna, which he had called cheap. These numbers may not hold for a particular workload, since the index is one evaluator's own mix of tasks.

stories.headline: OpenAI adds cache breakpoints and prewarming to GPT-6 prompt caching
stories.standfirst: The company said the changes raise hit rates and cut latency, and that reasoning changes no longer throw away a cached prefix.
body: OpenAI said it has changed how prompt caching works for GPT-6, adding higher cache hit rates, new diagnostics, explicit breakpoints and prewarming. The company published the changes on Tuesday evening, hours after launching GPT-6 Sol and Luna.

Rohan Paul, who summarises AI papers and releases, said the point is long-running agents that resend instructions, tool definitions and context on every turn. OpenAI's own page frames the changes the same way, as controls that reduce latency and cost.

The figures are not there. OpenAI's announcement names the features without putting a number on the hit-rate gain, the latency saving or the discount on cached tokens. Neither account gives a figure, and the paper has not tested the behaviour.

Prompt caching cuts what a developer pays to resend the same prefix, so the changes may matter most to agent builders running long tool loops. Whether the higher hit rates arrive in practice rests on OpenAI's description, which is the only account of them so far.

stories.headline: Rabbit releases cloud agent that runs without its R1 device
stories.standfirst: The company said OS3 runs in the cloud but acts locally on Windows, Mac and Linux machines, and Wired had the story first.
body: Rabbit is rolling out a standalone AI agent that does not need the company's R1 hardware, The Verge reported on Tuesday. Rabbit calls it OS3, an "agentic operating system" that runs in the cloud while operating locally across Windows, Mac and Linux devices.

Wired had the story first, according to The Verge, which credited the earlier report. The Verge called the R1 underwhelming in its own description of the company. Rabbit's claims about what OS3 can do are the company's own.

No price, no launch date and no model provider appear in the summary the paper has. Rabbit has not published figures on what OS3 costs or which models it calls, and neither outlet's account of the rollout gives a start date.

Agent products that run across a user's own machines raise the question of what permissions they hold on the machine. Neither account describes what access OS3 asks for, and Rabbit has not published that detail. The paper has not run it.

stories.headline: Vals AI scores Ant Group's Ling 3.0 Flash Fin at 54.9% on finance test
stories.standfirst: The evaluator put the model fourth among open-weight entries and said it costs $0.045 per task, the cheapest in the top 20.
body: Vals AI said Ant Group's Ling 3.0 Flash Fin scores 54.9% on its Finance Agent v2 benchmark, at $0.045 per task. The evaluator ranked the model fourth among open-weight entries and 16th overall, and called it the cheapest in the top 20 by a wide margin.

Vals AI put the score within one point of GPT-5.6 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5, at roughly 25 to 75 times less per task. Those comparisons come from the evaluator's own runs, according to its posts, and the paper has not reproduced them.

The model is specialised, not stronger overall, Vals AI said. LegalBench falls from 79.7% to 68.7%, MedScribe from 80.9% to 75.6% and MedCode from 32.3% to 29.3%. The evaluator did not name the model those declines compare with, and gave no dates for the runs.

Long-horizon coding is where the model falls away, on the evaluator's numbers. It scores 3.4% on Vibe Code Bench, 2.9% on Code Migration and zero on HLAB. Vals AI gave no figure for how rivals score on those three.

Open-weight finance models that price this low could change what a bank pays for routine analysis, if the scores hold outside one evaluator's harness. Neither Ant Group nor Vals AI has published the task mix behind Finance Agent v2.
